verses.verse:
तर्क बुध्या यथा जीवा नेश्वरम् प्रप्नुवन्ति हि।
तथा गणितमात्रेण बुधा जानन्ति न स्वरान।४४।
verses.text: Just as living beings do not reach God through the reasoning intellect, so the wise do not know the svaras through calculation alone.

verses.verse:
स्वरेश्वरौ समौ लोके व्याप्तौ सर्वत्र व्योमवत्।
ताल कालौ तथैवास्तः सूक्ष्मात् स्थूलौ च वन्हिवत।४५।
verses.text: In the world svara and Īśvara are alike, pervading everywhere like the sky; tāla and kāla (time) are likewise, [passing] from the subtle into the gross, like fire.

commentary.text: This proves that what is bhāvagamya (known through feeling) is not buddhigamya (known through the intellect). From the earlier figure it is established that the lowest note of the bānsurī, for which no hole other than the mukharandhra (mouth-hole) is needed, is the Pañcama of the mandra saptaka (lower octave), P̣a; and on this basis the holes of all the notes can be placed. In this, first, to find the middle Pañcama, we divide the length from the mouth-hole to the middle Pañcama in the ratio of 2-3, and fix the place of middle Pañcama at 2/5 from the mouth-hole. But if the pipe is only 6 times as long as its girth, or 5 and a half times as long, then in making its bānsurī the place of Pañcama will need to be 3/8. Although between 2/5 and 3/8 there is so fine a difference that it can be evened out by enlarging or reducing the roundness of the hole, still this fineness is necessary for a special situation. The remaining notes will be placed in the way described earlier. If someone wants to place the 12 notes by dividing the length from P̣a to Pa into 12 equal parts, the bānsurī will be out of tune. But if the pipe is tapered like a shehnai, the bānsurī may come out right. This same point was written by the late Śrī Bhātkhaṇḍe ji: (uparyupari saṅkocastvākāśe bhavati dhruvam) [going higher and higher, a contraction surely occurs in the space]. Now, below, the length and width of the bānsurīs from kālī 1 (first black key) to kālī 8 are written. Although harmoniums differ from one another by half a note or so, still some help can be had from this estimate. Here each length is 10 times its paridhimāna (measure of the inner circumference); but measured from the mouth-hole it will be 9 times. Just as the middle Pañcama, on the basis of mandra Pañcama and the mouth-hole, has been set not exactly midway between the two but between 2 and 3, in the same way it will be more suitable if the Ṣaḍja lying between the two Pañcamas is also not placed exactly in the middle but moved a little up towards Re; otherwise the mandra Pañcama will have to be made a baddha pañcama (bound Pa). If the last end of the pipe, which has been given the name mandra P̣a, is in its natural state, it is called mukta pañcama (open Pa). And if it is narrowed from inside with some ring, or more pipe is joined on beyond it and a large hole is made at the place of Pañcama, it is called baddha pañcama. Knowing of such a situation beforehand, skilled makers leave some part of the pipe or bamboo at the bottom and place mandra Pañcama [there]; if they do not do this, they divide the distance between P̣a and Pa into 13 equal parts and place Ṣaḍja between 6 and 7. The following śloka tells of these very two kinds of mandra Pañcama.
